primary.outcome_definition: Change From Baseline in the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) Clinical Summary Score (CSS)

outcome_definition_source.description_verbatim:
The KCCQ is a 23-item, participant self-administered questionnaire that assesses impacts of heart failure "over the past 2 weeks" on the following 7 domains:

* Physical Limitation (6)
* Symptom Stability (1)
* Symptom Frequency (4)
* Symptom Burden (3)
* Self-Efficacy (2)
* Quality of Life (3)
* Social Limitation (4)

Each of the 23 individual items are answered on Likert scales of varying lengths (5, 6, or 7-point scales).

KCCQ-CSS includes the symptom and physical limitation domains of the KCCQ. Scores are obtained by averaging the associated individual items and transforming the score to a 0 to 100 range. Higher scores indicate better health status.

Least Square (LS) mean was determined using ANCOVA model with Baseline + HF Decompensation Within 12 Months of Screening + T2DM Status + Baseline BMI group (\<35, \>=35 kg/m2) + Treatment (Type III sum of squares) as variables .
outcome_definition_source.components_as_the_registry_states_them: a continuous KCCQ primary AND 'First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Heart Failure (HF) Outcomes'. The 29 and 52 stored here DO correspond to that event co-primary.
outcome_definition_source.analysis_set_as_the_registry_states_it: The event co-primary is a first-occurrence composite.

primary.poolable_reason: TWO OF THE THREE TRIALS ON THIS PAGE REGISTER ONLY CONTINUOUS PRIMARY OUTCOMES, AND THIS PAGE POOLED EVENT COUNTS. Verbatim: STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM each register two co-primaries, 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and 'Change in Body Weight'. Both are CONTINUOUS CHANGE SCORES. Neither is an event count and neither can produce a 2x2 table. The counts stored for STEP-HFpEF DM, 7 of 310 against 18 of 306, CORRESPOND TO NO REGISTERED PRIMARY OUTCOME OF THAT TRIAL. SUMMIT is different and is the only row here with a defensible source: it registers a continuous KCCQ primary AND 'First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Heart Failure (HF) Outcomes', and its stored 29 of 364 against 52 of 367 do correspond to that event co-primary. So the pool joins one trial's registered event composite to another trial's unregistered counts. SEPARATELY: THE OUTCOME NAME AND THE MEASURE DESCRIBE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. The outcome is named 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and the stored measure is an ODDS RATIO. A change score has no odds. SEPARATELY AGAIN, AND IT IS WHY THIS TOPIC WAS INVISIBLE: THIS PAGE'S CARD WAS INVISIBLE TO OUR OWN TOOLING. The card existed and published 'HR 0.41 (0.22 to 0.79), k=3' -- a measure, a value and a trial count that all differ from the object's OR 0.4846 (0.3178 to 0.7389) at k=2. It was reported as having NO CARD because two scripts matched card links with the pattern [A-Z0-9_]+\.html, which cannot match the lowercase 'p' in HFpEF. A page invisible to the tool that counts pages is worse than an uncounted one: it is counted as a different thing, and this card escaped card-alignment checking entirely for as long as those tools have run.

pooled.withdrawn_note: WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: NOT that incretin therapies do not help in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. STEP-HFpEF, STEP-HFpEF DM and SUMMIT all report benefit on the outcomes they were designed around -- symptom burden measured by KCCQ, and body weight -- and SUMMIT additionally reports its heart-failure event composite. The trials here measure symptom scores and weight, and nothing on this page estimated those. WHAT IS CONFIRMED: SUMMIT's stored counts ARE its registered event co-primary, and all three identities are correct. THE REPLACEMENT QUESTION IS AVAILABLE AND PARKED: all three trials share a KCCQ clinical-summary-score primary, so a MEAN DIFFERENCE synthesis of symptom benefit is squarely defensible and needs no estimand judgement -- only each trial's least-squares mean difference read from its results record. That is the second such case in this programme, after BOCOCIZUMAB_LIPID.

kccq_css_change.poolable_reason: THIS IS A REPLACEMENT, NOT A CORRECTION. The withdrawn estimate on this page was an ODDS RATIO over event counts, and two of the three included trials register ONLY CONTINUOUS co-primaries. But ALL THREE register the SAME continuous outcome -- change in the KCCQ clinical summary score -- so a symptom-benefit analysis needs no estimand judgement at all. IT IS POOLED AT k=2, NOT k=3, AND THAT IS THE HONEST NUMBER. STEP-HFpEF DM's ClinicalTrials.gov record carries NO RESULTS SECTION, so this project has no registry-sourced value for it. Its published KCCQ difference exists in the literature and is NOT USED HERE, because every value on this page is read from a registry results record and importing one from elsewhere would break that guarantee for the sake of a third data point. THE TWO VALUES ARE THE REGISTRY'S OWN: STEP-HFpEF 7.8 (4.8 to 10.9) over 243 against 237, and SUMMIT 6.9 (3.3 to 10.6) over 301 against 313. POOLED: MD 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77) points on the KCCQ clinical summary score, k=2, 1,094 participants. Q = 0.14 on 1 degree of freedom, I-squared 0 per cent -- the two trials agree almost exactly.

THE TWO VALUES ARE THE REGISTRY'S OWN: STEP-HFpEF 7.8 (4.8 to 10.9) over 243 against 237, and SUMMIT 6.9 (3.3 to 10.6) over 301 against 313. pooled.caveats: WHAT A READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) k=2 AND THE INTERVAL SHOWN IS THE WALD ONE. At two studies a Hartung-Knapp interval uses a t-distribution on ONE degree of freedom and gives 1.80 to 13.06 -- far wider, and arguably the honest interval at this k. It still excludes no effect. Both are recorded. (2) HETEROGENEITY IS ZERO HERE, which at k=2 means the two trials agree, not that the finding is general. (3) THE THIRD TRIAL IS MISSING FOR A PROVENANCE REASON, NOT A CLINICAL ONE. STEP-HFpEF DM would very likely move this estimate very little; it is left out because its registry record has no results, and that is a rule about where numbers may come from rather than a judgement about the trial. (4) SUMMIT'S REGISTRY RECORD LABELS ITS CONTRAST 'Median Difference (Net)' while its arm values are least-squares means whose difference is 6.83. The label and the quantity disagree IN THE REGISTRY. The reported value is used and the discrepancy is stated rather than resolved. (5) A SEVEN-POINT KCCQ DIFFERENCE IS A SYMPTOM BENEFIT, NOT AN EVENT REDUCTION. Five points is the usual threshold for a clinically meaningful within-patient change. Nothing here estimates an effect on death or hospitalisation -- SUMMIT registers a heart-failure event co-primary and this analysis does not use it.

A symptom benefit, NOT an event reduction

replacement_analysis_2026_08_18.why_the_earlier_refusal_does_not_carry: This figure was refused earlier, on the ground that every number in this object was registry-sourced and breaking that for one data point costs the guarantee that makes the rest checkable. That reasoning was about an UNSOURCED import. The source is now identified, quotable and tiered, and the mixed provenance is declared per trial rather than hidden. The refusal was right about an unsourced number and does not extend to a sourced one.
replacement_analysis_2026_08_18.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that the two trials are free of bias -- no RoB-2 assessment is recorded. NOT that tirzepatide and semaglutide are interchangeable: this pools TWO DIFFERENT INCRETIN AGENTS against placebo on one instrument, which is a decision about the question being asked and is visible on the face of the topic. NOT that the abstract figure equals the full-text table figure.

is_this_a_class_question.answer: YES, AND THE TITLE IS WHAT MAKES IT SO. This topic is titled "Incretin therapies in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction" -- plural, class-level -- and the page asks a class question. Pooling tirzepatide with semaglutide is therefore the question the page exists to ask, not a combination smuggled into a drug question.
is_this_a_class_question.why_the_test_is_the_title_and_not_the_di: Disclosure does not make an incoherent pool coherent. Four cardiology topics closed on exactly this point -- not whether the combination was disclosed, but whether the question the PAGE ASKS is the question the POOL ANSWERS. Had this been titled for one agent, declaring the second would not have fixed it; the title would have had to change, as AZILSARTAN's did.
is_this_a_class_question.what_the_pool_does_not_establish_about_t: IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH THAT THE CLASS IS HOMOGENEOUS. I-squared is 0% and tau-squared is zero, and AT k=2 THAT IS WEAK EVIDENCE OF AGREEMENT RATHER THAN STRONG EVIDENCE OF IT: with two studies a heterogeneity statistic cannot distinguish genuine similarity from insufficient data to detect a difference. The two point estimates (6.83 and 7.30) are close, which is consistent with a class effect and does not demonstrate one. A reader should take this as a class-level estimate of TWO agents, not as evidence that incretins behave alike on this instrument.

published_synthesis_comparison.identity_verified_how: FROM THE DOCUMENT, not the filename and not the description it arrived with. published_synthesis_comparison.THIS_IS_NOT_A_REPRODUCTION_CHECK: READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING ANY NUMBER. Their outcome is CLINICAL HEART-FAILURE EVENTS -- a composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure. Ours is the KCCQ CLINICAL SUMMARY SCORE, a symptom and physical-limitation instrument. Their trial set is four; ours is two; THE OVERLAP IS EXACTLY ONE TRIAL. These are two syntheses over partly-overlapping trials asking DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. They cannot confirm or contradict each other's estimates, and setting their hazard ratio beside our mean difference would be a category error, not a check.

trial_set_overlap.note: SUMMIT is absent from their analysis because it tests TIRZEPATIDE and theirs is a semaglutide analysis. STEP-HFpEF (NCT04788511) is in theirs and not in ours. One trial in common out of five distinct trials.

NO KCCQ RESULT IS REPORTED. Our STEP-HFpEF DM input therefore REMAINS a publication-abstract value, the mixed provenance of this pool is UNCHANGED, and the supersession by a published results table REMAINS OWED.
published_synthesis_comparison.what_it_does_do_for_our_identity_check: The registration identity was previously checked in ONE DIRECTION only -- from the registry to the trial -- because the NEJM paper could not be opened. This paper prints, in its own abstract, that STEP-HFpEF DM is registered as NCT04916470. That is an INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED SOURCE tying the trial name to the registration, which strengthens the identity materially. IT IS STILL NOT the check that was wanted: it does not establish which NCT is printed on the NEJM paper the 7.3-point figure was quoted from. That remains unverified.

their_inclusion_logic_recorded_neutrally.what_they_did: All participants from the two STEP-HFpEF trials, and from SELECT and FLOW only those with an INVESTIGATOR-REPORTED history of HFpEF.
their_inclusion_logic_recorded_neutrally.denominators: 3743 of 22282 randomised participants, 16.8%. By trial: SELECT 2273 of 17604 (12.9%); FLOW 325 of 3533 (9.2%); STEP-HFpEF 529 of 529 (100%); STEP-HFpEF DM 616 of 616 (100%). So two trials contribute WHOLE and two contribute a SELECTED SIXTH AND ELEVENTH of themselves.
their_inclusion_logic_recorded_neutrally.precision_about_what_was_post_hoc: THE PAPER IS MORE SPECIFIC THAN 'A POST-HOC SUBGROUP' AND THE DISTINCTION IS WORTH KEEPING. It states that analyses of heart-failure outcomes within the HFpEF population of each trial were PRESPECIFIED in the statistical analysis plans of SELECT, STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM, and done POST HOC in FLOW; and that THE POOLING OF THE FOUR WAS POST HOC. Three of four subgroup analyses were prespecified; the pooling was not.
their_inclusion_logic_recorded_neutrally.investigator_reported_not_adjudicated: The HFpEF history is investigator-reported. The paper also reports a SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS using investigator-reported rather than adjudicated heart-failure events across all four trials, and states results were consistent.
their_inclusion_logic_recorded_neutrally.the_authors_own_caution: 'This pooled analysis was post hoc, and so should be considered to be exploratory.' Quoted from their Discussion. This is the authors' characterisation of their own work, not ours of theirs.
their_inclusion_logic_recorded_neutrally.why_this_is_recorded_at_all: Not as criticism. It is recorded because a reader who sees a four-trial participant-level pooled analysis will reasonably assume four whole trials, and here two of the four contribute a selected minority of their participants. The denominator is the fact; the judgement is the reader's.

published_synthesis_comparison.what_this_comparison_does_not_establish: NOT that our pooled KCCQ estimate is right or wrong -- their paper does not report the quantity we pool. NOT that semaglutide and tirzepatide behave alike on heart-failure events; their analysis contains no tirzepatide. NOT that a symptom-score benefit implies an event benefit, or the reverse: that inference is not licensed by either synthesis and neither paper claims it.
